chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Khalid ibn Abi Isma'il, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man prays facing the Qiblah while on top of Abu Qubays.' He said, 'There is no harm (in it).'

key_terms.أَبُو قُبَيْسٍ: Abu Qubays, a prominent hill/dome in Mecca near the Masjid al-Haram
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray on top of Abu Qubays in Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the physical elevation of the dome of Abu Qubays does not invalidate Salah, as the Imam confirms 'there is no objection' to praying there while facing the Qiblah. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that the validity of prayer depends on the purity of the place and the direction of the Qiblah, rather than the specific height or landmark status of the location, distinguishing it from later debates regarding the Kaaba's dome.
